where_disconnected: talonx_piv/session_runner.py, SessionRunner.process_tick() -- the earlier Task 65 commit (10a4c6a) fetched bars, fed SessionReadinessValidator, and updated staleness tracking, but never called any strategy evaluation or PaperLifecycle.order_intent(). The comment in that version read: 'No decision path is called here -- see module docstring. Signals/orders are zero today by construction, not by chance.'
why_disconnected: ORPB_V1 (talonx_quant/orpb_v1.py + orpb_v1_shadow.py) is the only strategy in the repository with a reusable, self-contained live-bar-driven decision+exit controller (OrpbV1ShadowController), but ORPB_V1 was independently REJECTED at Task 63P (docs/research/TALONX_RESEARCH_LEDGER.md) and is retired. Driving it against live 2026 market data today, even framed as 'plumbing only', would functionally be a forbidden ORPB replay -- any resulting paper trades would be attributable to a rejected strategy's exact logic running live.

The actual still-live, non-rejected strategy (talonx_quant/strategy.py, evaluate_signals(), invoked by consumer.py's QuantScanner) has no reusable live-bar-driven entry/exit controller of its own -- it only computes and attaches QuantSignal fields (stop_price/target_price/confluence_score/risk_reward_ratio/trend_aligned); consumer.py applies further publish-gating and talonx_paper.consumer.PaperTradingEngine (a completely separate module, driven by ActionableAlert events from talonx_core, several hops downstream of a raw QuantSignal) does the actual entry/exit simulation.

Correctly wiring talonx_quant/strategy.py into a live Alpaca-IEX-fed PAPER PIV session in one session required: (1) replicating talonx_quant.buffer.RollingBarBuffer's 1-minute bar buffer and its 120-bar (~2h) min_bars_required warm-up before compute_indicators() returns anything, (2) faithfully reusing -- not reimplementing from a cold read -- consumer.py's confluence/risk-reward/trend-alignment/cooldown publish-gating so the wired path represents the actual live decision logic rather than a looser approximation of it, and (3) writing a new, from-scratch entry/exit/position tracker for strategy.py signals, since none exists (unlike ORPB_V1's OrpbV1ShadowController). Under the original session's time pressure, this was judged too much new, untested decision logic to introduce into a live financial pipeline without a lower-risk fallback in hand.

The resolution taken in Task 65B (this task) is Part C/D of this same document: restore the real strategy.py flow properly, with consumer.py's actual gating logic reused via direct import (see decision_engine implementation notes below), plus an explicit, safety-bounded PIV_LIFECYCLE_PROBE fallback so full order-lifecycle coverage does not depend on a natural signal firing during the live session.
paper_order_generation_route_before_this: NONE. talonx_piv/lifecycle.py's PaperLifecycle.order_intent() existed and was fully order-lifecycle-tested (Task 64, 22 focused tests) but nothing in the runtime path called it -- it was only ever invoked directly from unit tests.
smallest_safe_change: Add talonx_piv/decision_engine.py: a NEW, PIV-namespaced module that (a) maintains a per-symbol pandas DataFrame bar buffer matching talonx_quant.buffer.RollingBarBuffer's schema, (b) calls talonx_quant.indicators.compute_indicators(df, config) unmodified, (c) calls talonx_quant.strategy.evaluate_signals(...) unmodified, (d) reuses consumer.py's exact publish-gating thresholds/logic (imported, not reimplemented) to decide whether a QuantSignal is actionable, and (e) tracks the resulting entry/exit itself against subsequent bars (stop_price/target_price from the QuantSignal, EOD flatten) since no reusable tracker exists for this strategy.

Wire SessionRunner.process_tick() to call this decision engine only for READY symbols (unchanged Part F/L readiness gating), and to submit resulting entries/exits through the existing, unmodified PaperLifecycle.order_intent().

No change to talonx_quant/strategy.py, indicators.py, consumer.py, config.py, fprc_v1.py, or orpb_v1.py themselves -- every one of those modules is imported read-only. Zero drift verified via git diff before and after.
